newMachineStartupSequence: Pull the latest reviewed origin/main and resolve all paths from the new repository root.
Read the authoritative documents and complete objective in the stated order.
Confirm the source Goal is paused, the source daemon is absent and source automations are stopped; then determine the single intended production owner before starting any scheduler.
Install and verify interpreters, repository-contained dependencies, four isolated browser posts and the WeCom native UI provider without copying session credentials.
Run read-only repository integrity, dependency and release checks; run only isolated synthetic tests that cannot reach production events or groups.
Revalidate the four posts by real business domain and visible business text, including login, captcha and risk overlays; do not infer health from process or URL alone.
Verify original queue, ledger, cursor and deduplication identities before starting the director.
Transfer or recreate the same complete Goal only once, then transfer all five automations exactly once after ownership readback.
Start the new director as the only production controller and verify real PID, startup identity, heartbeat, control, live_steps and locks.
Use the next legitimate scheduled runs for real new-machine acceptance; documentation, tests and old-machine receipts are insufficient.
cutoverGates: The source Goal is paused and the source thread performs no further Goal work.
There is no in-flight production step, group lock, physical post lease or unclaimed UI task that can be duplicated.
Old and new schedulers are never active as production owners at the same time.
The new machine has its own valid login state and visible UI capability.
Goal and all five automations have exactly one verified owner.
New-machine runtime health and normal business receipts are independently verified.
stopAndEscalate: Stop the affected post for login, QR scan, captcha, account risk or user-required authorization.
Keep independent safe work moving when one post is externally blocked.
Do not retry any send whose result is attempted, unknown or missing send count.
If cutover state is ambiguous, keep production fenced and report the exact ownership evidence; do not guess.
